findings.text: Register name lookup uses a small table pairing a human readable name with a byte displacement inside the architecture tracer register capture. Entries cover low numbered general registers plus conventional aliases for frame base, link, stack pointer and program counter. Displacements are derived from layout offsets of the capture structure at build time.

A query service maps a register name to its byte displacement by scanning the table for an exact name match and returning the associated displacement. An unknown name yields a negative invalid argument indication.

Call site normalization converts a compiler emitted patch address into the address of the call slot to be rewritten. The conversion depends on build family, handling a legacy direct form, a form with one post entry slot, and a form with two pre entry literal slots plus an optional target identification slot and a post entry slot. Misaligned input triggers a rate limited warning and a zero result, and unexpected pre entry content triggers a rate limited warning while continuing.

Symbol resolution performs the inverse mapping from a call slot address back to its function start. Without pre function literals the start lies one unit earlier. With pre function literals the distance is one or two units depending on presence of a target identification instruction, examined with a fault tolerant read when near a page boundary, returning zero on read failure.

Text patching optionally validates current content before writing. When validation is requested the existing word is read through a safe accessor and compared to expectation, distinguishing read failure from mismatch. The new word is then written through a no sync patch primitive, with patch failure reported distinctly from validation failures.

Global tracer target update is a no operation when per site call operations are enabled. Otherwise it constructs a link branch from the central call trampoline toward the supplied destination and installs it without validation of prior content.

Direct branch reach spans one hundred twenty eight mebibytes forward and backward from the patch site, and instruction addresses must be word aligned. Patch calculations advance in units of one fixed width instruction.

Distance computation rejects endpoints that are not word aligned and distances outside the supported window, reporting the limit value and emitting a diagnostic in either failure case. Valid distances are returned as signed differences.

Branch encoding produces a fault sentinel when the requested distance is out of range or the branch flavor is unrecognized. For recognized link and no link flavors it combines the appropriate base pattern with a word scaled twenty six bit displacement.

Module trampoline selection chooses between regular and initialization trampoline areas based on the address region of the patched site, yielding no trampoline when modules are disabled or the address lies elsewhere. A separate reachability check reports whether a destination lies within the direct branch window of a site using signed difference.

Callable address resolution prefers the requested destination when directly reachable, substituting the generic trampoline when a custom destination is out of range. Out of range cases require module context, resolved safely when not already known, and then use the module trampoline for the site region. Resolution fails when module support is absent, owning module cannot be established, or no trampoline exists for the region.

Per record operation association selects a unique operation when per site handling is enabled and valid, falling back to the global list operation otherwise. The selected pointer is persisted as a sixty four bit literal at an eight byte aligned location twelve bytes before the record address. Clearing and refresh helpers either store the nop or current association or do nothing, depending on build family.

Literal persistence serializes against concurrent patching by holding the dedicated patch spin lock with local interrupts masked across the whole update. The target is accessed through a fixed temporary mapping, written with a fault tolerant copy, then unmapped before releasing the lock and restoring interrupt state. The copy status is returned to the caller.

Call site life cycle centers on refreshing the stored operation association, resolving a reachable destination, and installing the new instruction with validation of prior content. Module initialization prepares the preceding slot to preserve the return address in a scratch register, creation converts a placeholder into a link branch, modification converts one link branch into another, and removal converts a link branch back into a placeholder. A legacy module path without argument capture installs the placeholder without validation, and a global update helper marks the operation as sleep capable before rewriting all sites.

Register move construction is expressed as a logical operation with a zero source and no shift. Logical encoding validates the operation mnemonic and the operand width, enforcing shift limits appropriate to thirty two or sixty four bit forms and setting the wide form indicator. Register insertion validates the register number and field role, propagating the fault sentinel on error and otherwise placing a five bit value at the role specific position.

Function return tracing entry points first honor a per task pause indicator and do nothing while paused. Otherwise they capture the current return location and frame context and delegate to the graph enter service, replacing the saved return location with the common handler only when entry succeeds. One form operates on explicit addresses and another extracts frame and return slots from the register capture.

Graph caller activation toggles a single call site between a placeholder and a direct branch toward the graph trampoline, validating prior content in both directions. Dedicated enable and disable wrappers expose the two directions and propagate the patch status.

A processor state save helper is gated on floating point support and expects a non preemptible context. When active it preserves user vector state and then clears processor vector state while local interrupts are masked.

Power management handling idles in a registered notifier with three outcomes. Entry into low power triggers the save and clear helper and reports success, exit from low power reports success without action, and failed entry or unknown commands report completion without action. Registration occurs during early init in one build family and is omitted in the other.

Processor offline handling clears the per processor pointer to last vector state and reports success. Hotplug registration for this handler occurs during early init in one build family and is omitted in the other.
Processor enablement for vector handling turns on floating point access for privileged and unprivileged levels in the architectural control register and then enforces ordering with a barrier.

Early vector initialization runs once at boot. When floating point is present it registers power and hotplug handlers, otherwise it logs absence. It separately logs absence of advanced vector support when missing, initializes extended vector control interfaces, and always reports success.
A single static instance of user vector state is reserved for firmware call handling, with kernel private linkage and zero initialized content at boot.

Primary boot entry establishes machine state before enabling virtual memory. It records entry conditions, preserves firmware arguments, installs an early stack, builds an identity map, ensures cache coherence appropriate to whether entry occurred with memory management enabled, determines the boot exception level, performs processor setup including translation controls, and transfers to the primary switch routine.

Hazards include patching the wrong location after misaligned or unexpected pre entry content, faulting on page edge reads without tolerant access, corrupting executable text without validation, losing vector state across power transitions or processor offline without save and clear, and executing stale mappings or cached boot code without the required invalidate or clean sequence.

Register operands occupy five bit fields within the instruction word at bit positions zero, five, ten and sixteen according to destination, base, extended and operand roles. Logical immediates use a six bit shift field and branch displacements use a twenty six bit word scaled field.
Vector save and clear holds local interrupts masked across the user save and processor clear sequence, preventing interruption between the two steps on the local processor.
